rules.title: No class/new/delete; heap = Box
rules.statement: Node codes 93-95 (CLASS decl / NEW_EXPR / DELETE_STMT) are retired and no longer produced by the grammar. The language has no `class` item, `new` expression, or `delete` statement; heap allocation goes exclusively through `Box<T>`.

rules.title: Chained comparisons rejected
rules.statement: A run of 2+ comparison operators in one expression (`a < b < c`) parses as CHAINED_CMP; sema rejects it with a diagnostic suggesting `a < b && b < c`.

rules.title: Paren-wrapped type unwraps to inner
rules.statement: A parenthesized type expression `(T)` (PAREN_TYPE) is structurally equivalent to `T`; sema unwraps it to the inner type.

rules.title: &&T / &&mut T resolve to nested single refs
rules.statement: `&&T` (DOUBLE_REF_TYPE) resolves as a REF_TYPE wrapping a REF_TYPE; `&&mut T` (DOUBLE_REF_MUT_TYPE) resolves as a REF_TYPE wrapping a MUT_REF_TYPE. Both are sema-level rewrites of a single lexed double-`&` token, not a distinct type former.

rules.title: Bare [T] is unsized; legal only behind a pointer or as ?Sized subst
rules.statement: A bare `[T]` type expression (UNSIZED_SLICE_TYPE) produces Kind::UnsizedSlice and cannot appear by value; it is only legal behind `&`, `*const`, or `*mut` (where resolve canonicalises it back to SLICE_TYPE / Kind::Slice) or as the concrete type substituted for a `T: ?Sized` parameter.

rules.title: Tail expression synthesizes implicit return
rules.statement: An expression with no trailing `;` at statement position (TAIL_EXPR) is sugar: sema synthesizes an implicit `return expr` for functions with non-void return type.

rules.title: Byte-string literal lowers to [u8; N] array literal
rules.statement: A byte-string literal `b"..."` (LIT_BYTES) carries the raw token text including the `b"…"` envelope; sema decodes escapes and lowers the literal to an `[u8; N]` array literal of the decoded byte length N.

rules.title: Char literal denotes a Unicode scalar value
rules.statement: `'X'` (LIT_CHAR) carries the original char-literal text including quotes; sema decodes it to a Unicode scalar value (not a raw byte).

rules.title: IIFE / expression-as-callee call
rules.statement: `(expr)(args)` (INVOKE_EXPR) allows an arbitrary expression, not just a name, in callee position; RECEIVER is the callee expression, ARGS the argument list. Sema routes the call through closure-call or fn-pointer-call resolution depending on RECEIVER's type.

rules.title: break/continue/return are value-position expressions
rules.statement: `break`, `continue`, and bare `return` may appear in expression position (BREAK_EXPR, CONTINUE_EXPR, RETURN_EXPR), each carrying Rust's `!`/Never type; sema lowers each to its statement form (SBreak/SContinue/SReturn) plus an Error-typed sentinel expression so the surrounding type-check accepts the position. RETURN_EXPR in this form takes no value.

rules.title: Nested fn lifts to a top-level free function
rules.statement: `fn name(params) [-> T] { body }` at statement position (NESTED_FN) is sema-lifted: the body becomes a top-level free function under a gensym'd name, and the local name is bound as a fn-pointer `let`.

rules.title: union: struct-shaped, max-of-fields layout, unsafe field access
rules.statement: `union NAME { f1: T1, f2: T2, … }` (UNION_DEF) is sema-treated as a Struct-shaped type with `is_union=true`; layout is the max size across fields, aligned to the max field alignment; every field-access expression on a union requires an enclosing `unsafe` block.

rules.title: static: one true global per item; mut requires unsafe
rules.statement: `static [mut] NAME: T = expr;` (STATIC_DEF) emits one `llvm.mlir.global` per item with a stable address (`&STATIC` has stable identity). The `mut` form additionally requires `unsafe` at every read and write. Omitting `= expr` declares an extern-linkage global (extern-block declaration).

rules.title: offset_of! yields a compile-time i64 byte offset
rules.statement: `offset_of!(Type, field)` (OFFSET_OF) resolves Type, walks its ABI layout to `field`, and emits an `i64` constant equal to the field's byte offset within Type.

rules.title: sizeof...(T) yields pack length as u64
rules.statement: `sizeof...(T)` (SIZEOF_PACK) is a value-position expression whose evaluation yields the length of type-parameter pack `T` as a `u64`.

rules.title: Float-literal pattern parses but is rejected at sema
rules.statement: A float literal in match-arm pattern position (PAT_FLOAT) is grammatically accepted but rejected by sema (float equality patterns are not permitted).
rules.uncertainty: Rejection logic itself lives outside this slice; only the grammar-level comment attests it.

rules.title: String-literal pattern lowers to an str_eq guard
rules.statement: A string literal in match-arm pattern position (PAT_STR) is sema-lowered to a `str_eq` guard against the scrutinee rather than a structural pattern match.

rules.title: let-pattern destructuring is refutability-checked
rules.statement: `let <pattern> = expr;` beyond a simple identifier/tuple binding (LET_PAT) requires sema to check the pattern is irrefutable; sema lowers the binding via an internal match.

rules.title: Destructuring assignment into existing places
rules.statement: `(a,b)=e`, `[a,b]=e`, and `S{a,b}=e` (DESTRUCTURE_ASSIGN) destructure into pre-existing places (not new bindings); sema desugars to a synthetic `let __da = rhs;` followed by one assignment per named place. A general postfix-chain lvalue not covered by the specialised write productions (`a[i][j]`, `(*p).0`, `m.f[i].g`, PLACE_ASSIGN) instead lowers directly to `deref_write(&mut <place>, rhs)`.

rules.title: if-let chains desugar to sequential refutable binds
rules.statement: `if let P1 = e1 && let P2 = e2 && cond { THEN } else { ELSE }` (IF_LET_CHAIN, segments LET_CHAIN_LET/LET_CHAIN_COND) desugars to a flat sequence of refutable pattern binds and boolean-condition checks; the chain falls through to ELSE as soon as any segment fails (bind mismatch or false condition), short-circuiting the rest.

rules.title: extern block ABI defaults to children without an override
rules.statement: `extern "ABI" { extern_fn_def* }` (EXTERN_BLOCK) applies its ABI string as the default for every contained EXTERN_FN that doesn't specify its own ABI override; omitting the block's ABI string literal means the default Logos-internal ABI. sema_collect splices the block's items into the module-level item stream with this default applied.

rules.title: use {..} last-segment case disambiguates variant vs sub-package
rules.statement: `use pkg.Path.X.{V1, V2, …};` (USE_VARIANTS) disambiguates the grouped braces by the case of the last dotted segment (TYPE_NAME): an uppercase first character means enum-variant bare-name shorthand (X is an enum, V1/V2 its variants); a lowercase first character means a grouped sub-package import (X is a package, the braces list sub-names).

rules.title: #![attr] is a distinct module/file-level inner attribute
rules.statement: `#![name]` / `#![name(args)]` / `#![name=val]` (INNER_ANNOTATION) is file/module-scoped, structurally identical in payload to a per-item ANNOTATION but tagged with a distinct CODE so sema can separate module-level attributes (e.g. `#![no_implicit_prelude]`) from item-level ones.

rules.title: metacall runs a compile-time callee and splices its result
rules.statement: `metacall <call_expr>` (METACALL, expression position) is an explicit compile-time invocation. At item position, `metacall <call_expr>;` (METACALL_ITEM) is JIT-executed by the driver; the callee must return a QuoteItemBlob, which is spliced into the surrounding item stream via `logos_emit_item_blob_subst`. After splicing, the node is rewritten to METACALL_ITEM_DONE, which sema's item-dispatch silently skips (and which is never produced by parsing).

rules.title: quote_item!/quote_expr!/quote_ty! are typed AST literals
rules.statement: `quote_item! { item* }` (QUOTE_ITEM), `quote_expr! { expr }` (QUOTE_EXPR), and `quote_ty! { type }` (QUOTE_TY) are typed AST-literal forms yielding, respectively, an item list, a single expression AST (root carries a schema_type_code), and a Type AST. Inside a quote body, `#(body)sep*` (REPEAT_GROUP) repeats `body` with separator `sep` in {none, comma, `&&`}. `$ident` in type position (ANTIQUOT_TYPE) is legal only inside `quote_ty!` and refers to a Type-valued binding; `$ident...` in a type-argument list (ANTIQUOT_PACK) is legal only inside `quote_ty!` and refers to an `Array<Type>`-valued binding.

rules.title: Function-style macros exist in expression and item forms
rules.statement: `name!(args)` / `name![args]` (FN_MACRO_CALL, expression position) resolves CALLEE against `#[fn_macro]`-annotated functions, passing each argument AST as an ExprBlob. `name!{...}` at module-item position (FN_MACRO_CALL_ITEM) has the same callee/args shape but routes through the metacall_item-style splice path (callee returns an ItemList / QuoteItemBlob); after splicing the node becomes FN_MACRO_CALL_ITEM_DONE, which sema skips.

rules.title: Doc comments accumulate and attach to the following item
rules.statement: Outer doc-comment lines `/// text` (DOC_LINE_LIT) and outer block comments `/** ... */` (DOC_BLOCK_LIT, envelope + per-line leading `*` stripped) accumulate across consecutive occurrences and attach as one joined string to the next real item's DOC slot. Inner forms `//! text` (INNER_DOC_LIT) and `/*! ... */` (INNER_DOC_BLOCK_LIT) instead accumulate into the enclosing module's summary (`module_inner_doc`), not into any item.

rules.title: &tagged<TS> Trait: tag-dispatched thin pointer
rules.statement: `&tagged<TS> Trait` (TAGGED_TYPE) denotes a thin (single-word) pointer to a trait object whose concrete implementation is selected by a tag drawn from the type-set `TS`, as opposed to a fat (vtable-carrying) `&dyn Trait` pointer.
rules.uncertainty: Only the node-code comment is in this slice; dispatch mechanics (how TS maps tag→impl) are implemented elsewhere.

rules.title: instantiate Foo<T>; pins a monomorphization root
rules.statement: `instantiate Foo<T>;` (INSTANTIATE_DECL) pins TYPE=`Foo<T>` as a pre-instantiation monomorphization root; an optional IS_PUB marks it as a library-site re-export so downstream crates get the instantiation without repeating the declaration.

rules.title: <type:T> embeds a Type as a first-class Writ value
rules.statement: `<type:T>` inside a Writ `@`-literal (WRIT_TYPE_LIT, NAME = bare type identifier) is sema-embedded as a first-class Writ Type value, i.e. a type usable as ordinary literal data rather than only in type position.
rules.uncertainty: Comment marks this "slice 1: IDENT only" — the grammar accepted here may not cover the full type-expression surface for this position.

rules.title: WritStatic type-arg literal has byte-hash const identity
rules.statement: A nested Writ literal at type-argument position, `Foo::<@{...}>` (LIT_WSTATIC), is sema-lowered to `ConstVar(WritStatic, hash)`: two occurrences with byte-identical literal content share identity via that hash, i.e. const-generic identity for WritStatic args is structural/byte-hash-based, not by-reference.

rules.title: <type:CFG.SLOT> extracts a type from a WritStatic slot
rules.statement: A type-position expression `<type:CFG.SLOT>` (CFG_SLOT_TYPE, NAME=CFG ident, KEY=slot ident) extracts the type stored at top-level slot SLOT of WritStatic const-generic parameter or type alias CFG. Monomorphization resolves this to the slot's `<type:T>` value once CFG becomes a concrete WritStatic.

rules.title: IDENT::<TARGS> at expression position
rules.statement: `IDENT::<TARGS>` at expression position (GENERIC_REF, CALLEE=ident, TYPE_PARAMS=type_arg_list) names an explicitly-instantiated generic item (function or associated item) as a first-class expression-position reference, independent of any surrounding call.

rules.title: Byte-string pattern reserved but not lexer-wired
rules.statement: A byte-string literal in match-arm pattern position (PAT_BYTES) is a reserved node code; per the source comment, lexer support for producing it is still pending.
rules.uncertainty: Marked "reserved, lexer support pending" in-source — feature may not be reachable from surface syntax yet.

rules.title: Char-literal and char-range patterns decode to u32 scalar
rules.statement: A char literal in match-arm position, `'A'` (PAT_CHAR, VALUE=original token text), and a char range, `'a' ..= 'z'` (PAT_CHAR_RANGE, LHS/RHS=original endpoint token text), are both sema-decoded to `u32` Unicode scalar values for matching.

rules.title: dyn Trait + Send/Sync + 'a auxiliary bounds
rules.statement: A trait-object type may carry auxiliary bounds after the principal trait: `+ Send`/`+ Sync`-style auto-trait bounds (AUTO_TRAIT_BOUND, NAME=bound ident) and `+ 'a` lifetime bounds (AUTO_LIFE_BOUND, NAME=lifetime label). Both collect into the dyn_type's ITEMS array alongside type-args; `resolve_type` buckets bounds vs args by CODE. Auto-trait bounds are folded into the TraitObject TypeRef's const_val bits and enforced at unsize-coercion sites; lifetime bounds are currently only logged, not enforced, pending region-inference wiring.
rules.uncertainty: Lifetime-bound enforcement explicitly stated as not yet implemented ("sema currently logs but does not enforce").

rules.title: Nested combinator inside annotation argument list
rules.statement: An annotation argument list may nest a combinator call, e.g. `#[cfg(all(unix, target_arch = "x86_64"))]` (ANNOT_CALL, NAME=head ident such as `all`/`any`/`not`, ARGS=nested annot_args list of further ANNOT_CALL / ANNOT_KV / bare-NAME entries), i.e. annotation argument syntax is recursive, not flat.

rules.title: schema: typed view over a WMap-backed Writ object
rules.statement: `schema S : code(expr)? { name: type = key, … }` (SCHEMA_DEF, FIELDS=SCHEMA_FIELD_DEF array, optional CODE_EXPR) is sema-registered as a Struct with exactly one synthetic backing field `m: *const WMap<Wu6,WAny>` and `is_schema=true`; the declared fields exist only in a key/type side-table, not as real struct fields. Each SCHEMA_FIELD_DEF (NAME, TYPE, optional VALUE=key const-expr) defaults to positional index when VALUE is absent.

rules.title: schema enum: closed union over schemas by schema_type_code
rules.statement: `schema enum E : category(expr)? { V(S), … }` (SCHEMA_ENUM_DEF, FIELDS=VARIANT_DEF array each NAME=variant/TYPE=concrete schema, optional CODE_EXPR) is a closed union over `schema` types, discriminated at runtime by the pointee object's schema_type_code.

rules.title: typeof(expr) as a type-position expression
rules.statement: `typeof(expr)` (TYPEOF_TYPE, VALUE=expr AST) is usable in type position and denotes the compile-time-resolved type of `expr`, without evaluating `expr` at runtime.

rules.title: Annotation arguments: key=value, positional, and array-literal forms
rules.statement: An annotation's argument list admits three leaf shapes: `NAME = literal` key-value (ANNOT_KV), a bare positional literal (ANNOT_POS), and an array literal `[literal, …]` (ANNOT_ARR, ITEMS=literals).

rules.title: Writ literal scalar and container node shapes
rules.statement: Writ `@{...}`/inner `{...}` map literals (WRIT_MAP), `@[...]`/inner `[...]` array literals (WRIT_ARRAY), and scalar leaves for string (WRIT_STR), integer (WRIT_INT), float (WRIT_FLOAT), bool (WRIT_BOOL), and null (WRIT_NULL) values are distinct AST node kinds; each map entry is a WRIT_ENTRY key:val pair.

rules.title: Typed dense array/map literals and negative-int literal
rules.statement: `@<ElemType>[v,...]` (WRIT_TYPED_ARRAY, TYPE=elem name) and `@<K,V>{...}` (WRIT_TYPED_MAP) are typed variants of the array/map literal forms, distinct from the untyped WRIT_ARRAY/WRIT_MAP; `@-42` or an inner `-42` inside an array/map (WRIT_NEG_INT) is a distinct node from WRIT_INT for the negated-literal case.

rules.title: $x and ${expr} capture forms in Writ literals
rules.statement: `$x` (WRIT_CAP_IDENT, NAME=var name) captures a variable by name inside a Writ literal; `${expr}` (WRIT_CAP_EXPR, VALUE=expr) captures the value of an arbitrary host-language expression at the same position.

rules.title: <ElemType>[] and <K,V>{} Writ type expressions
rules.statement: `<ElemType>[]` (WRIT_ARR_TYPE, TYPE=elem name) and `<K,V>{}` (WRIT_MAP_TYPE, TYPE=key/RET_TYPE=val) are type-expression syntax describing, respectively, a typed Writ array's element type and a typed Writ map's key/value types.

rules.title: Writ-literal list and map comprehensions
rules.statement: `@[elem for x in iter (if guard)?]` (WRIT_LIST_COMP) and `@{k:v for x in iter (if guard)?}` (WRIT_MAP_COMP) mirror the general LIST_COMP/MAP_COMP comprehension shapes but produce Writ array/map literal values instead of host list/map types.

rules.title: Writ-literal pattern forms in match arms
rules.statement: Writ literals participate in pattern position with dedicated node kinds mirroring the literal forms: `@null` (PAT_WRIT_NULL), `@true`/`@false` (PAT_WRIT_BOOL), `@<int>`/`@-<int>` (PAT_WRIT_INT, IS_NEG flag), `@"..."` (PAT_WRIT_STR), `@{k: pat, ...}` (PAT_WRIT_MAP, ITEMS=PAT_WRIT_MAP_ENTRY list each with KEY/VALUE), `@[pat, ...]` (PAT_WRIT_ARR, ITEMS=sub-patterns), `@<T>[..]` (PAT_WRIT_TYPED_ARR, TYPE) and `@<K,V>{..}` (PAT_WRIT_TYPED_MAP, TYPE/RET_TYPE?) match on the typed-array/typed-map's declared type rather than on element contents.

rules.title: genos declaration is a trait with is_genos=true
rules.statement: A `genos` declaration (GENOS_DEF) is sema-represented as an ordinary trait definition with the flag `is_genos=true` set, i.e. it shares the trait-definition data shape rather than introducing a separate item kind.
rules.uncertainty: Only the node-code comment is present in this slice; genos-specific semantics beyond the flag are implemented elsewhere.

rules.title: Bare { } block is a scoping statement
rules.statement: A bare `{ stmts... }` block appearing at statement position (BLOCK_STMT, BODY=block) introduces a nested scope without being an `if`/`loop`/`fn` body or any other control-flow construct.

rules.title: List and map comprehension expressions
rules.statement: `[elem for x in iter (if guard)?]` (LIST_COMP: VALUE=elem, NAME=x, ITER=iter, GUARD?=guard) and `{k: v for x in iter (if guard)?}` (MAP_COMP: adds KEY=k, VALUE=v) are expression-position comprehensions that iterate `iter`, bind `x` per element, optionally filter by `guard`, and produce a new list or map respectively from the (filtered) elements.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: Python-style comprehensions; not present in Rust.
